summary: Backend: 21/22 pytest passed. Frontend: All primary flows verified (home, products, category filters, coming-soon, product detail + waitlist submit, register->/account, admin login, admin dashboard stats+list+audit, admin create+delete via modal, theme toggle, legal pages, 404, contact form). Only real issue: brute-force lockout doesn't trigger because identifier includes request.client.host and the ingress rotates between multiple internal IPs.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout is INEFFECTIVE behind the ingress. `check_lockout`/`record_failed` key on `f"{request.client.host}:{email}"`, but in the deployed environment request.client.host is the internal proxy IP (10.81.21.4, 10.81.21.6, ...) which rotates per request. Six consecutive wrong-password attempts split across proxies produced counts of only 3 per key, so no 429 was ever returned. The task explicitly requires 429 after >=5 fails.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout keying: use X-Forwarded-For (first hop) or key solely on email so the counter is not split across ingress replicas. Example: `ip = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or (request.client.host if request.client else 'unknown')` — or simply `identifier = email` for account lockout.
critical_code_review_comments: Rate-limit identifier uses request.client.host which is the proxy IP behind ingress; use X-Forwarded-For or key by email only.

seed_products() overwrites `status` and `featured` on every startup via $set — any admin edits to seeded slugs will be reverted on next backend restart. Consider using $setOnInsert for all fields, or a `seeded_at` guard.

get_current_user calls ObjectId(payload['sub']) without try/except — a malformed sub in a forged/legacy token would raise bson InvalidId (500) instead of a clean 401. The catch-all handler masks this as generic 500.
Global @app.exception_handler(Exception) swallows every unexpected error as opaque 500 with no logging — makes production debugging harder; log exc_info before returning.
Waitlist endpoint silently swallows all Exception on insert as 'duplicate' — non-duplicate DB errors will falsely report success.
CORS allow_origins hardcodes production URL alongside env-driven FRONTEND_URL; acceptable but consider env-only.
Password reset token is printed to stdout ([PASSWORD RESET] ...) — acceptable for dev but must be gated for production.
server.py is a single ~700-line file; consider splitting into routers/auth, routers/products, routers/admin, models, seed.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py. All product/auth/admin/waitlist/contact/search endpoints verified. Only failing test: test_brute_force_lockout — root cause is documented above; not a test bug. All frontend data-testid selectors used in the spec exist and work. Admin modal fields expose data-testid admin-field-slug, admin-field-name, admin-field-short_description, admin-field-category, and save button admin-form-save.
rca of the issue: Symptom: 6 consecutive wrong-password POSTs to /api/auth/login all return 401, never 429. RCA: `record_failed(identifier)` uses identifier=`f'{request.client.host}:{email}'`. Behind the K8s ingress, request.client.host is the internal proxy IP which load-balances across multiple values (observed 10.81.21.4 and 10.81.21.6). Attempts are therefore distributed across two separate identifiers, so neither reaches count>=5 within the 15-minute window. Mitigation: honor X-Forwarded-For or key the lockout counter on email only (recommended for account-lockout semantics), or on the first XFF hop for IP-lockout semantics.
